scores.quote: As a result of MCLR reduction and our active effort on repricing existing borrowings, our cost of borrowings declined further by 18 b ps

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — MSME credit (30%+ of GDP, largely unserved by banks) and affordable housing where penetration is ~11-12% and 90% of incremental demand by number is affordable.
scores.quote: even the incre mental 90% demand is coming from affordable housing

scores.rationale: Purely organic build with no acquisitions, a 100% secured book, conservative LTVs, escrow-based construction finance, a self-imposed 20% cap on CF mix, and low leverage of 2.8-3.3x.
scores.quote: we will remain guided by our cautious risk management strategy to keep its mix at/or below 20% of consolidated AUM

scores.rationale: Promoter-led management set out a multi-year platform rebuild and an INR300bn AUM by FY27 target and has tracked it through cost-heavy loss-making years in gold loans and technology before the payoff arrived.
scores.quote: 4 years ago, we made a deliberate structural choice to move away from being a traditional NBFC ... to becoming a plat form native AI-first financial institution

scores.rationale: Management is not celebrity-driven but the recent calls are notably promotional — repeated 'highest ever', best-in-industry NPA and 'highest among all NBFC peers' ESG claims dilute a pure substance-over-profile read.
scores.quote: Capri Global has achieved an S&P ESG score of 71, the highest among all NBFC peers

scores.rationale: Scale hiring (1,000 gold staff at launch, 13,066 employees) and Great Place to Work certification show people investment, but senior turnover (CFO Chakraborti to Lodha, multiple chairmen in five years) and no articulated succession pipeline offset it.
scores.quote: Capri Loan continues to be "Great Place To Work" certified for a third year in a row

scores.rationale: Generally candid — disclosed the gold-loan drag on profit, elevated cost-to-income, the co-lending 'learning curve', and pre-warned of a co-lending slowdown from new guidelines — though answers on cash-disbursement mix were evasive.
scores.quote: there could be a temporary slowdown in co -lending volume for a couple of quarters

scores.rationale: Strong FY26 results (PAT +98%) coincide with a gold price surge, falling rates and co-lending fee recognition, so skill cannot yet be cleanly separated from favourable conditions in a book grown 60% in one year.
scores.quote: In the context of rising gold prices, we maintained conservative loan-to-value ratios

scores.rationale: One genuine niche leadership claim exists in the car-loan distribution platform where it says it is the leading pan-India non-dealer corporate DSA, though core lending products carry no such position.
scores.quote: even today, the corporate DSA s who are not dealers, we are #1 pan -India, and we are having a dominant position in this pace

scores.rationale: Branch density in underserved districts gives local advantage and MSME LAP borrowers are somewhat sticky, but gold and housing borrowers face low switching costs and there is no captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: we firmly believe a strong branch network is essential to ou r business

scores.rationale: The segments are fragmented and contested by aggressive banks, NBFCs and fintechs, with management itself conceding intense competition for quality construction-finance projects.
scores.quote: The competition amongst lenders for quality projects i s inten se

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are low beyond licensing — banks are lending aggressively down-market, fintechs are entering origination, and pricing power had to be 'returned' rather than being structurally held.
scores.quote: given bank s are extremely aggressive - still cont inue to be aggressive here

scores.rationale: A large informal/unorganised lending pool and bank-unserved thin-file borrowers provide clear share to take, which is exactly the segment CGCL targets.
scores.quote: we cater to entirely different segments where customer s are smaller unorganized and do not possess adequate income through paper work

scores.rationale: This is no longer an ignored niche — the company actively courts global rating agencies, ESG raters and analysts, and its high-growth gold/MSME segments attract heavy bank and NBFC capital.
scores.quote: secured credit rating from 2 leading global rating agencies ... by Fitch Ratings and Ba3 Corporate Family Ratings ... by Moody's

scores.rationale: Yields of ~16.3% reflect borrower segment risk rather than brand-driven pricing power, and there is no evidence of image or taste-based demand.
scores.quote: driven by increasing share of high -yield products and decline in cost of funds

scores.rationale: In gold loans, where the customer is handing over personal collateral, management explicitly credits trust alongside demand and backs it with best-in-industry 0.3% GNPA and disciplined LTVs.
scores.quote: Gold loan AUM saw robust growth to INR16,965 crores ... led by healthy customer demand and trust

scores.rationale: Convenience is the core proposition — 1,429 branches with direct feet-on-street, sub-30-minute gold loan TAT, 60-second pre-approved top-ups and 85 lakh app engagements in FY26.
scores.quote: products like Gold Loan have a turnaround time of less than 30 minutes and our preapproved top-up loans are disbursed in 60 seconds

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail/self-employed (6.9 lakh customers, 74% self-employed in housing) and the benefit offered — speed, proximity, doorstep access — is correctly matched to that type, though without intangible or lock-in reinforcement.
scores.quote: Our growth remains granular, diversified and retail led with our customer base now exceeding 6.9 lakhs

scores.rationale: A genuinely deep, in-house multi-product stack (Orion LOS, SPARK, Pegasus, proprietary SSLM) delivering measurable operating leverage, but in lending this is an efficiency edge that larger rivals can fund and replicate rather than a durable exclusion.
scores.quote: We have built and deployed our own specialized small language model, SSLM, that is domain trained model, purpose -built for financial services use cases in India

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists; the 35+ lender and 14 bank partnerships are procurement and distribution relationships that do not strengthen with each additional borrower.
scores.quote: We added 15 new lender relationships this year, taking the active relationship now to 35 plus

scores.rationale: Distribution is the company's strongest real asset — 1,429 own branches plus a pan-India car-loan platform across 14 banks being leveraged to cross-sell insurance — but it remains well short of the reach of established gold and housing incumbents.
scores.quote: we have built a scalable platform with pan -India network in this segment with potential to monetize further for distribution of other products

scores.rationale: Massive, clearly growth-oriented capacity build — transformers from ~17-20,000 MVA to 65,000 MVA in a year with 110,000 MVA planned, a ₹748 crore greenfield switchgear plant and the ₹7,584 crore OSAT project — while consolidated ROCE stayed 20-33% and Power ROCE was cited above 100%.
scores.quote: just one year back we were at some 18,000, 17,000 MVA capacity for transformer, today we are almost close to 65,000 MVA

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

R&D is yielding a visible pipeline — AMX next-generation drives launched, 400 kV GIS on schedule for FY27 commercialization, IE3/IE4 motor portfolio, KAVACH and Vande Bharat propulsion — but several programs (EV truck motors, KAVACH approvals) are still unconverted after years.
scores.quote: for 400 kV GIS the plan is exactly on the schedule there... 2027 financial should see the commercialization happening

scores.rationale: The Axiro/Renesas RF semiconductor acquisition plus CG Semi is a large, complex, out-of-core bet that has depressed consolidated margins (₹111 crore FY26 semiconductor drag, 89 bps), the opposite of a bolt-on where post-deal OPM improves; only the small G.G. Tronics is profitable at ~₹100 crore revenue.
scores.quote: total semiconductor segment impact of 111 Cr, 89 bps

scores.rationale: Distribution policy is minimal — a ₹1.3 interim dividend — while the company raised ₹3,000 crores of equity via QIP (shrewdly at a strong valuation, but the opposite of buybacks) with the proceeds still parked in other financial assets.
scores.quote: approved the payment of interim dividend of INR1.3 per equity share

scores.rationale: Returns are high (standalone ROCE 22-35%, FCF 119% of PAT in Q1) but the business is heavy manufacturing in a big capex phase with receivables up ~50% against 20% sales growth, so it is capital-intensive rather than asset-light.
scores.quote: return on capital employed annualized for the quarter was 35%

scores.rationale: Motors grew 8-10% against a flat-to-negative industry and management explicitly says the HT motor served market is small with room to expand, alongside power order intake far outpacing the industry.
scores.quote: our served market is very small. We are serving a smaller portion of the market

scores.rationale: Export execution is credible and delivering: a $99.2 million US hyperscale data-centre transformer order (largest in company history) after two years of key-account work, export order bookings up >50% in nine months and more than doubled for the year, plus motor GTM and service centres in Africa and Europe.
scores.quote: For exports, has gone up by more than 50% in the last 9 months

scores.rationale: Power growth is heavily price/realization-led (378 bps and 287 bps margin expansion on better price realization) and motors is roughly 50/50 price and volume, but Industrial margins fell on adverse mix and un-passed commodity cost.
scores.quote: 378 basis points margin expansion driven by improved price realization

scores.rationale: LT motors appear to be bottoming after several negative quarters, but the far larger power/transformer business is well into an upcycle rather than near its bottom, with the run visible only to ~2029.
scores.quote: It was negative, if you look at the data. It has crossed the bridge of being flat or a little better

scores.rationale: End markets — grid/T&D capex under the new NEP, hyperscale data centres, railway signalling and domestic semiconductor packaging — are in secular expansion with structural capacity shortfall to 2029.
scores.quote: even if you compare only with India-India, in 2029, this still will be a shortfall

scores.rationale: Expansion is overwhelmingly organic and equity-funded (₹3,000 crore QIP) with capacity added ahead of demand, but the semiconductor diversification is a large non-core bet that dilutes the organic-focus case.
scores.quote: it will not be a knee-jerk reaction. As we get more stronghold on our pipeline, it keeps swelling, we will keep adding capacity

scores.rationale: The landmark US data-centre order was the product of two years of deliberate vertical/key-account work, and management repeatedly frames capacity and export builds on a five-year horizon rather than reacting to headlines.
scores.quote: We have been working on this for last 2 years religiously on these key account management, the vertical focus

scores.rationale: Calls are business-detail heavy with delegation to business heads and refusals to forecast, though the CEO does slip into promotional flourishes like "Amrit Kaal for power sector" and "my aspiration is much bigger".
scores.quote: the market recovery, I cannot forecast

scores.rationale: A deep bench of named business heads presents on every call with orderly succession in the railway VP role, and the company is explicitly investing in a semiconductor talent pool and senior GTM leadership.
scores.quote: continued investment in the talent pool for semiconductor business

scores.rationale: Management openly flags the LT motor market deterioration, inability to fully pass on commodity inflation, the railway PVC shortfall and its own first-time delay on KAVACH approvals, but withholds routine detail like export splits, backlog margins and IE3 mix.
scores.quote: there was a delay in initial approval because we are also doing it for the first time

scores.rationale: Headline results are inseparable from a once-in-a-decade transmission upcycle — Power PBIT margin rose to 21.9% while the more skill-dependent Industrial segment saw margins fall from 12.1% to 9.9% — so skill cannot yet be cleanly separated from cycle.
scores.quote: PBIT was at INR613 crores which is 9.9% of the sales as against INR707 crores, 12.1% in the previous year

scores.rationale: CG is the acknowledged LT motor price-setter whose increases competitors follow, indicating a strong mind-share position, though this is leadership in a contested market rather than a monopoly.
scores.quote: LT Motors, we are the market leaders. So we got to define what should be the pricing in the market

scores.rationale: Customized transformers, utility/railway vendor qualification and multi-year approval cycles create real switching costs, but the cancelled CLW KAVACH order after a lapsed 12-month delivery window shows the lock-in is not absolute.
scores.quote: none of these transformers are standard transformers. They're customized to the customer

scores.rationale: Transformers/EHV is a few-player industry running sold out with customers asking for more supply, though railways remains a reverse-auction tender business where the customer holds pricing power.
scores.quote: what we keep hearing, give us more, give us more. I don't think anybody is saying stop it

scores.rationale: Transformer manufacturing takes 24-36 months to stand up and pricing behaviour is rational (order intake not chased on price; competitors followed CG's 5% motor hike), offset by peers adding capacity and potential Chinese re-entry.
scores.quote: we are not compromising on margins to get more orders

scores.rationale: CG grew motors while the industry was flat-to-negative and competitors followed rather than undercut its price hike, implying weaker players ceding ground, though no specific donor is named.
scores.quote: after we increased our pricing by 5%, the good news is lot of competitors are following what we are doing

scores.rationale: CG is the opposite of under-the-radar — an intensely covered large cap fielding IIFL, JP Morgan, UBS, Kotak, Jefferies and Motilal on every call, with a QIP oversubscribed more than three times.
scores.quote: It was oversubscribed by more than 3x and saw the participation from Indian and global marquee investors

scores.rationale: There is some brand-based pricing authority in LT motors, but gross margins are visibly hostage to commodity inflation that could not be passed on, which is inconsistent with image-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: lower gross margin in motors due to significant commodity inflation that could not be passed on entirely to the market

scores.rationale: The US data-centre win was explicitly on reliability, efficiency and uptime rather than price, and management names quality/standards/reliability as the sole differentiator in winning export business.
scores.quote: transformers specifically engineered to meet the stringent reliability, efficiency and uptime requirements

scores.rationale: Distribution and service intimacy are being actively built — overseas service centres, channel partners and senior GTM leaders on the ground — with visible order-intake improvement, but this is a work in progress rather than an established edge.
scores.quote: with our GTM getting activated now with the senior leaders in place, in fact we see improvement in the order intake

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate/utility (PowerGrid, Techno Electric, Indian Railways, US hyperscalers) and CG matches it with reliability, customization and qualification-based lock-in rather than consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: a large order for supply and servicing of 765 kV transformer package from Power Grid Corporation

scores.rationale: Capability spans 765 kV (soon 1,200 kV) transformers, RF semiconductor design and 98-99% OSAT yields, but several tech fronts are catch-up rather than lead — 400 kV GIS not yet commercialized, EV truck motors still in development, IE3+ portfolio incomplete.
scores.quote: today, we are operating at about 98%, 99% kind of yield, which is a good situation

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is discussed anywhere in the calls.

Domestic reach underpins LT motor price leadership and the company is deliberately pairing exports with local service centres because service is vital, but the international network is still being assembled.
scores.quote: when you are exporting motors, you also need to have service centres there. And that's what Marais and team is busy setting up

scores.rationale: Sustained, rising growth capex (INR15bn over 7 quarters in FY25 rising to ~INR30bn planned for FY27-29) with explicit 18-20% ROCE targets and funding from internal accruals while net debt fell.
scores.quote: we have outlined a planned capex of approximately INR30 billion over FY '27 to FY '29... These investments are expected to generate a ROCE of 18% to 20%

scores.rationale: Only fleeting marketing mentions around the new Athiva launch, with brand equity largely residing with licensed operators (Marriott, Taj, Hyatt, Ritz-Carlton) rather than Chalet's own A&P.
scores.quote: We did multiple marketing activities during this period to create market awareness

scores.rationale: No R&D discussion anywhere in the 16 calls; not applicable to an owner-operator of hotel real estate.

Deals are small, simple, complementary asset/land bolt-ons bought with approvals in place to cut execution risk (Goa land, Udaipur resort at INR1.71bn for 144 keys), though acquired resorts are currently margin-dilutive at ~43% occupancy.
scores.quote: We completed the acquisition of Udaipur Resort... a total consideration of INR1,710 million for 144 key resort spread over 8.2 acres of land, reducing the land to launch risk substantially

scores.rationale: No dividend or buyback policy is ever discussed; capital flows the other way via the April '24 QIP and a minority equity dilution at the DIAL subsidiary, with all cash reinvested.
scores.quote: the Board has approved a onetime proposal for a minority equity shareholding in just one of our projects

scores.rationale: Deliberately asset-heavy model — owned hotels, 2.4mn sq ft of offices, residential development — with ~INR28bn revenue against a very large owned asset base plus INR8.3bn of non-yielding CWIP, so asset turn is structurally low despite location moats.
scores.quote: Our strategy of hard asset-led capacity addition and operational efficiency places us in a sweet spot

scores.rationale: Small share of a fragmented Indian market with keys rising from 3,389 to over 5,000, and evidence of beating the market on RevPAR in MMR in Q3 FY26, though Mumbai underperformed the industry in Q4 FY26.
scores.quote: Chalet now has 3,389 operating keys with a pipeline of approximately 1,655 keys across 7 assets

scores.rationale: Credible domestic expansion beyond the Mumbai base into Delhi airport, Hyderabad, Goa, Udaipur, Khandala and Rishikesh, but execution has slipped repeatedly (Delhi DIAL pushed to Q4 FY27, Airoli held up on clearances).
scores.quote: We expect some delays at Taj project at Delhi International Airport due to ongoing pollution-led stoppages

scores.rationale: Growth is clearly rate/mix-led (Q3 FY26 RevPAR +12% on 16% ADR growth with occupancy down 230bps) and mix is upgrading toward luxury/resorts, though Q4 FY26 RevPAR fell 3% on a 7.7pp occupancy drop.
scores.quote: RevPAR growth close to 12%, driven by 16% growth in ADRs overall

scores.rationale: The company sat near the cycle bottom in FY23 but by FY26 is mid-to-late cycle, with Mumbai ADR growth of 0-2% and new supply pressure in micro markets like Navi Mumbai.
scores.quote: Mumbai saw ADR growth of only 0% to 2% and an occupancy decline of 0 to 2 percentage points

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion — rising incomes, experience-led consumption, infrastructure spend and MICE/weddings — with supply persistently lagging demand.
scores.quote: Travel and tourism is rapidly moving from being a discretionary spend to a way of life... supply growth has lagged demand in key segments and markets

scores.rationale: Predominantly organic/greenfield growth, no large transformative M&A, and INR19bn deployed over two years while net debt fell from INR25bn to INR19bn with ~INR15bn self-funded and borrowing cost cut to 7.48%.
scores.quote: net debt has reduced from INR25 billion as of March '24 to approximately INR19 billion as of March '26... approximately INR15 billion has been funded through internal accruals

scores.rationale: Multi-year projects are pursued through to completion against a stated 5-year plan (the Delhi airport hotel bid won in 2022 is still being staged to opening in FY27-28), showing tenacity though with timeline slippage.
scores.quote: if you look at our 5-year plan, our debt does come down very significantly by then

scores.rationale: Commentary is operational and metric-driven with no promoter celebrity or self-congratulatory framing; the MD transition was handled matter-of-factly on a routine call.
scores.quote: on behalf of the entire Chalet family, I congratulate him for his elevated role

scores.rationale: Seven consecutive years of Great Place to Work certification (ranked 4th and best hotel company in its category in 2022) and an internal succession of Shwetank Singh to MD & CEO evidence a real leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: we have been certified by Great Place to Work with above-industry benchmark scores for seventh year in a row

scores.rationale: Management openly owns misjudgements and discloses weak spots by asset — the election-impact admission, the Vashi RevPAR dip from new supply, Powai construction hurting occupancy, and project delays.
scores.quote: election impact took us by surprise, I must admit that. I got that wrong. I thought the impact will be minimal.

scores.rationale: Much of the record-setting performance traces to a post-COVID industry upcycle and a favourable supply-demand gap that management itself credits, so operating skill cannot be cleanly separated from the cycle.
scores.quote: buoyed by favourable demand-supply arbitrage

scores.rationale: Several assets hold near-unique micro-market positions — a Delhi hotel physically walkable from Terminal 3, the largest hotel in Bengaluru Whitefield, two properties inside the Hyderabad Mindspace park — but this is site-specific, not company-wide.
scores.quote: travelers can potentially just walk in from the terminal building into the hotel with their bags and trolleys

scores.rationale: Scarcity of comparable sites creates local quasi-monopolies (beachfront Goa, airport-adjacent Sahar/Delhi), though guests face essentially no switching costs.
scores.quote: the scarcity of seafront, beachfront assets is what is going to drive business for the acquisition opportunity that we have

scores.rationale: Indian hospitality is fragmented and contestable — a supply surge in Navi Mumbai directly cut Vashi RevPAR, and corporate/crew customers negotiate rates annually.
scores.quote: This was due to significant increase in room supply in similar category hotels in Navi Mumbai micro market

scores.rationale: High capital intensity, land scarcity and long approval cycles (environmental clearances, Goa approvals) keep supply lagging demand and pricing rational, but announced pipelines from domestic and global brands show entry is not closed.
scores.quote: there has been a healthy pipeline of signings by both domestic and global hotel brands, supply continues to lag behind

scores.rationale: Mixed evidence — Chalet beat the MMR market on RevPAR in Q3 FY26, but underperformed Mumbai in Q4 FY26, and no weak-competitor cohort is identified as a share source.
scores.quote: So, we've actually been outperforming the market on the whole.

scores.rationale: Chalet is a well-covered listed company fielding questions from Ambit, ICICI, Macquarie, Antique, IDBI and PhillipCapital, in an asset class attracting heavy institutional capital.
scores.quote: The next question is from the line of Sameet Sinha from Macquarie Capital.

scores.rationale: Premium positioning delivers high margins (hospitality EBITDA ~46-49%) and Athiva sustains ADRs above INR15,000, but the pricing image largely rides on licensed third-party brands rather than Chalet's own.
scores.quote: The pickup in occupancy with ADR sustaining north of INR15,000 gives us confidence

scores.rationale: A meaningful book is contracted, reliability-driven corporate business — airline crew contracts, MICE and wedding bookings made well in advance — where consistency matters more than headline rate.
scores.quote: we do have a lot of activity on the MICE segment because that gets booked out in advance

scores.rationale: Convenience is the core competitive asset: hotels adjoining airport terminals, inside office parks, and at a metro doorstep, giving accessibility rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: the metro at Whitefield is going to be launched sometime in December this year and the station from an office perspective becomes extremely convenient for us, which is literally at our doorstep

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched — location/TCO-driven corporate, crew and MICE demand in business micro-markets, and experience-led retail leisure in the newer resorts at Khandala, Rishikesh, Goa and Udaipur.
scores.quote: Compared to business hotels, resorts did very well during this quarter.

scores.rationale: No technology or product-development moat is discussed in any call.
No two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale effect is described anywhere in the excerpts.
Distribution and loyalty reach come from franchised operators (Marriott, Taj, Hyatt, Ritz-Carlton) rather than any Chalet-owned channel, so the advantage is rented, not proprietary.
scores.quote: The hotel will operate under the Ritz-Carlton brand.

scores.rationale: Sustained growth capex on the 240,000 TPA TAN plant (₹1,645 cr, commissioned FY26), energy-efficiency schemes at Gadepan and IMACID's P2O5 expansion from 5 to 7 lakh MT, but the TAN cost overran from ~₹1,200 cr with ~6-12 months delay and IRR is only a 'healthy double-digit'.
scores.quote: we have incurred a project expenditure of INR 1,184 crores out of the total estimated cost of INR 1,645 crores

scores.rationale: Seed-to-Harvest farmer engagement (1,200+ meetings, 700 demos, 43,000 soil samples) plus digital outreach (100,000 app downloads, YouTube Silver Play Button) has demonstrably converted into CPC/biologicals growth, though it is farmer-connect spend rather than durable consumer brand equity.
scores.quote: we undertook more than 1,200 farmer meetings, conducting over 700 demos and 124 soil sample days

scores.rationale: Consistent product output — 38 new molecules in five years contributing 25-30% of sales, 17 launches in FY26, 12-14 more planned for FY27, plus the CFCL-TERI Centre of Excellence with jointly-owned IP and global commercial rights — but most chemistry is in-licensed/generic rather than proprietary discovery.
scores.quote: Out of the 65 in the last five years, we have launched 38 new molecules which are contributing to 25% to 30% of sales

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were announced or discussed across the 15 calls; only a vague statement about 'exploring and evaluating capacity in India or abroad' with no deal, price or integration evidence to judge.
scores.quote: we continue exploring and evaluating capacity in India or abroad

scores.rationale: A steady but modest dividend (₹11/share for FY26 on PAT of ₹1,950 cr) alongside debt prepayment to zero net debt shows prudence, but there is no buyback, no articulated distribution framework and no valuation-linked capital-return discipline discussed.
scores.quote: Board of Directors has recommended a final dividend of Rs. INR 6 per share, totaling to Rs. 11 per equity share for FY '26

scores.rationale: Revenue of ₹20,794 cr against a heavy gas-based urea asset base plus chronically large subsidy receivables (₹1,954 cr at FY26-end, and a ₹3,000 cr borrowing spike in FY23) makes this capital- and working-capital-intensive, with returns set by policy rather than protected by a moat.
scores.quote: The major effect is because of the higher borrowing by about INR 3,000 crore

scores.rationale: Small shares across categories leave real runway (10% urea, 5% NPK/DAP, 3% CPC) and share is visibly being captured in the newer verticals — biologicals reached ~6% of market with volumes +31% and revenue +58%.
scores.quote: we are almost 3% of the crop protection chemicals and specialty nutrients business in the country

scores.rationale: Methodical expansion of CPC beyond the northern urea heartland into south and west India, with non-urea states already 8-10% of CPC sales and pan-India molecule licences, plus early export exploration for TERI biologicals — credible but still small.
scores.quote: there is a lot more that we have to go ahead with, both, in our existing core earlier geographies more in the north, as well as in the south and west geographies

scores.rationale: Headline growth is overwhelmingly volume- and government-price-driven — complex fertiliser revenue +175% on volumes rising from 5.64 to 12.31 lakh MT at only ~4% EBIT margin, with DAP a fixed-margin business — although mix is slowly improving toward the 23.5%-margin CPC segment.
scores.quote: DAP is a fixed margin business, despite the higher cost that we see

scores.rationale: The company is squarely mid-cycle rather than near a bottom with an identifiable upturn: after the FY23 trough it has enjoyed good years, and FY26 Q4 shows fresh input-cost pressure (ammonia $850-900, sulphur $900-950, LNG) with no clear turn called.
scores.quote: ammonia prices increased sharply to around $850 to $900 per ton while Sulphur prices also increased

scores.rationale: Indian agri-input demand is structurally supported — ₹1.71 lakh crore subsidy allocation, record 348 million tonne foodgrain output, a secular shift to balanced fertilisation and biologicals — though it is a mature, policy-capped end market rather than a fast secular expansion.
scores.quote: The Union Budget has allocated about INR 1.71 lakh crores to the Department of Fertilizers this year, providing long-term visibility and stability

scores.rationale: Purely organic build-out with no acquisitions, long-term loans prepaid to zero debt in FY25 even while funding the ₹1,645 cr TAN project, and continued investment through the difficult FY23 subsidy squeeze.
scores.quote: we have prepaid our long-term loans, and we have zero debt in the Company

scores.rationale: The TAN project was carried through cost escalation, geopolitical disruption and delay from FY23 announcement to FY26 commissioning, alongside a patient multi-year build of CPC, biologicals and now seeds, with an explicit 3-5 year view on earning innovator trust.
scores.quote: you need a three-to-five-year kind of comfort creation between the parties

scores.rationale: Calls are led by functional heads with plain operational detail and no promotional framing; management declines to hype unannounced plans rather than headline-chase.
scores.quote: Let me keep that a secret for the moment.

scores.rationale: A visible internal pipeline — Abhay Baijal moved CFO (FY22-23) to MD, and CFO succession ran through internal finance leaders Anand Agarwal (ex-VP Finance) and Anuj Jain (ex-AVP Finance) — plus dedicated business heads built for TAN before commissioning.
scores.quote: we have our people in place, a marketing team in place

scores.rationale: Consistently owns bad news — the FY23 one-time P&K loss and its arithmetic, unscheduled plant shutdowns and stripper leaks, the ₹31 cr labour-code hit — and refuses to guess on the unresolved Gadepan-III policy expiry, though the 'worst is behind us' framing in FY23 was somewhat optimistic.
scores.quote: We are not hazarding a guess as to what they will do. The numbers could vary from our estimate, both positively and negatively.

scores.rationale: Strong reported PAT growth (FY26 +18%) is substantially a function of subsidy policy, gas-price pass-through and monsoon rather than management skill, and the company itself frames earnings as dependent on government escalation mechanisms — so results should not be read as evidence of exceptional capability outside the CPC segment.
scores.quote: the government has compensated us on a base of a higher gas number

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position anywhere: urea and DAP MRPs are government-fixed, the CPC portfolio is admittedly ~75% generic chemistry with identical competing molecules, and there is no aftermarket or services annuity.
scores.quote: still in this country, 75% of sales is through generics CPC business

scores.rationale: Real regional density in Rajasthan/UP/Haryana/Punjab where freight economics and dealer entrenchment help, but there are no switching costs — farmers and dealers can change brands freely and only 8-10% of CPC sales come from outside the core belt.
scores.quote: the CPC sales are also coming from the non-Urea states also... it should be around 8% to 10%

scores.rationale: Not a favourable oligopoly — the effective price-setter is the government via MRP and NBS rates, new urea capacity (HURL's three plants, Matix) keeps arriving, and the company must lobby for interim relief rather than negotiate price.
scores.quote: can you give us interim relief pending final calculations

scores.rationale: Capacity keeps being added under government policy support and pricing is administratively determined rather than rationally set by the industry, leaving margins hostage to NBS rates and a 4%-of-MRP fixed DAP margin.
scores.quote: this will be a template not only for us, but for all other plants that will follow through. That is, Matix is there, HURL three plants are there

scores.rationale: In CPC/biologicals Chambal is taking share from weaker generic marketers by winning early access to innovator molecules and shelf space, being only the third company allowed a Nissan combination product.
scores.quote: we have launched a combination of that which has come from the house of Nissan, and we are only the third Company who has been allowed

scores.rationale: This is a widely-covered listed fertiliser major with regular analyst calls from Kotak, DSP, Nirmal Bang and others, and its TAN entry is into a visible, capital-attracting industrial chemicals market, not an ignored niche.
scores.quote: TAN is a very important focus area for CFCL, and vertical and horizontal expansions are being actively explored

scores.rationale: The bulk businesses have zero pricing power under fixed MRP and thin margins (complex fertilisers ~4% EBIT), offset partially by the Uttam-branded CPC/specialty portfolio which sustains ~23% EBIT margins on product reputation.
scores.quote: we were not able to pass on that price increase to the market because of the overall MRP pricing situation

scores.rationale: In the value-added segment farmers buy on demonstrated field reliability, with demos and trials converting into repeat purchase — Uttam Pranaam and Superrhiza have covered ~3 million acres since launch on that basis.
scores.quote: seeing is believing... the farmer tends to create repeat buy and once the repeat buy starts happening, then automatically volume growth and margin growth happens

scores.rationale: Direct farmer intimacy is the company's clearest customer advantage — Seed to Harvest demos and soil testing, an advance-placement strategy that occupies dealer shelf space ahead of competition, and a 100,000-download farmer app.
scores.quote: the more early you place them, you occupy the shelf, hence, you take care of the competition to an extent

scores.rationale: Customers are retail farmers and the company matches the benefit type correctly — brand trust, demonstrations, agronomy advice and channel access rather than TCO selling — evidenced by the Uttam brand family and digital farmer engagement.
scores.quote: Our emphasis on maintaining strong connect with both dealers and farmers continues

scores.rationale: A genuine operating-efficiency edge in ammonia/urea with repeated energy-saving schemes beating expectations, and now Casale state-of-the-art TAN technology plus jointly-owned TERI IP — but the core process technology is licensed rather than proprietary.
scores.quote: we are the most efficient manufacturer of ammonia as an entire complex in the country

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network exists in this business; the digital app and social channels are one-way outreach tools with no evidence of value increasing with user scale.
scores.quote: Our Chambal Uttam Krishak Mitra app crossed about 100,000 downloads

scores.rationale: The urea-anchored dealer network in the northern belt is being successfully leveraged to push CPC, specialty nutrients, biologicals and now seeds, taking that segment to ₹1,203 cr at ~23.5% EBIT margin, though the channel is only being built to ~30% depth and width and rivals have comparable reach.
scores.quote: the idea is to put a channel in place which can take care of around 30% of depth and width

scores.rationale: Capex is dominated by maintenance (Rs 200-300 cr/yr) with growth confined to the Rs 1,600 cr LOBS and Rs 400 cr retail outlet projects plus a 25% stake in a Rs 36,354 cr JV refinery whose incremental ROIC is unproven.
scores.quote: LOBS project, Group 2, Group 3 LOBS project is INR1,600 crores. The retail outlet project is INR400 crores... Besides, every year, you can assume another INR500 crores is our normal capex

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotion spend across any of the three calls — CPCL sells ~90% of output to Indian Oil at refinery transfer price.

No formal R&D line, but continuous process/product development yields new value-added grades (pharma-grade hexane, SAF trial, pentane, textile-grade MTO) — incremental refinery optimisation rather than genuine R&D.
scores.quote: we have launched trial runs of 2 new products. One is pentane, the other is textile grade MTO

scores.rationale: No bolt-ons; instead a single very large greenfield JV commitment (Cauvery Basin, Rs 36,354 cr, cost already revised up from Rs 31,500 cr) that is the opposite of small, simple and complementary.
scores.quote: The revised capital cost is at Rs. 36,354 crores with a 25:75 equity holding between CPCL and Indian oil respectively

scores.rationale: Dividends are consistently paid and scale with profits (Rs 5/share FY25 rising to a record Rs 62/share including a first-ever interim in FY26), but the policy is discretionary and there are no buybacks.
scores.quote: in addition to the interim dividend of INR8 per equity share of INR10 each, the Board has recommended a final dividend of INR54 per share, taking the total dividend for the year to INR62 per share

scores.rationale: Refining is capital-intensive and asset-heavy, but CPCL sweats an old fully-depreciated asset base at 111-112% utilisation, giving decent turns without a genuine protecting moat.
scores.quote: CPCL achieved a highest ever crude throughput of 11.71 MMT, million metric ton, which equivalents to 112% of installed capacity

scores.rationale: Some share opportunity from the southern MS deficit that CPCL is chasing, but ~90% of output is contractually tied to Indian Oil at RTP, so meaningful share capture is structurally constrained.
scores.quote: MS in southern market, there is a clear shortfall so, the production is less than demand. It is close to about 20 TMT per month

scores.rationale: No geographic expansion — the company is a single-site Manali refinery whose only new footprint is the Cauvery Basin JV within the same state, and exports are opportunistic rather than a strategy.
scores.quote: Export is not a compulsion to me. Export is one of the options available to me to optimize my margins and realization

scores.rationale: Prices are international-parity and outside management control, so growth comes from volume/throughput and modest mix upgrades (distillate yield 76%→79.1%, value-added products), not pricing power.
scores.quote: our prices are at international parity prices... the gross cracks I will be deriving from the market

scores.rationale: The cycle troughed in FY25 ($4.22/bbl GRM) and has turned sharply upward through FY26 ($9.2/bbl full year, $13.75/bbl in Q4), with limited new domestic capacity for two years.
scores.quote: The gross refining margin, GRM, for financial year 2025-'26 was $9.2 per barrel as compared to Singapore benchmark of $5.83 per barrel

scores.rationale: Indian fuel demand grows modestly (MS ~4-6%, HSD ~2.5-3%) but refining of fossil transport fuels is not in permanent secular expansion given the energy transition.
scores.quote: Like MS, they are projecting 6% and here we see around 4%-5%. HSD we see at 3% growth forecast, as against 2.5% odd here

scores.rationale: Leverage was cut hard (D/E 0.39 → 0.18 gross, 0.09 net) with capex funded internally and no acquisitions, though the off-balance-sheet Rs 2,570 cr JV equity commitment is a large concentrated bet.
scores.quote: Our debt equity stands at 0.18 at a gross level as compared to 0.39 last year... on a net basis, it is less than INR1,000 crores

scores.rationale: The multi-year fuel-and-loss/energy roadmap promised in 2023 was delivered step by step (F&L 9.06% → 8.51% → 7.73%; EII 89.2 → 87.4 → 84.0), but as a PSU subsidiary of IOCL, independence is limited.
scores.quote: if you remember our Energy Indexes and our Fuel and Loss Indexes were quite high 2-3 years back and we went to a roadmap where we said on a sustained basis, we will bring it down to very efficient levels

scores.rationale: Calls are led by the Director (Finance) with technical CGMs, focused on operating metrics, and management explicitly declines to comment on media speculation.
scores.quote: As for reacting to media reports, I may or may not be as well-informed as you.

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline in any of the three calls; the history shows frequent government-driven Chairman/MD turnover but the calls are silent on it.
Management gives precise numbers (inventory gains/losses, core vs reported GRM, forex loss), explains profit declines by naming cracks rather than excuses, and admits the limits of its own knowledge.
scores.quote: Dividend has come down because of the profits... The primary reason is the international cracks... that is not a specific phenomenon with respect to CPCL. That is the industry phenomena

scores.rationale: Record FY26 results are largely a crack-cycle upswing that management itself attributes to the market, so genuine skill is confined to the verifiable efficiency gains (F&L, EII, yield, Solomon first quartile).
scores.quote: What is sustainable is my efficiency, my flexibility, my realizing opportunities, but yes, the gross cracks I will be deriving from the market

scores.rationale: No monopoly in the customer's mind — products are commodity fuels sold at refinery transfer price — though niche grades like pharma-grade hexane and MTO give small pockets of specialisation.
scores.quote: close to about 90% of our product, mostly HSD, MS, goes to Indian Oil... the agreement is at RTP, that is refinery transfer price

scores.rationale: CPCL is the dominant refinery in a structurally deficit southern region with pipeline-connected logistics and an embedded IOCL offtake relationship, creating a regional/captive position rather than true switching costs.
scores.quote: the dispatches are happening to Indian Oil. And the facilities are located close to our plant

scores.rationale: Indian refining is a concentrated PSU-plus-Reliance oligopoly, but CPCL's single dominant customer (IOCL, its own parent) holds the negotiating power, as evidenced by reported demands for additional RTP discounts.
scores.quote: there was some news regarding the OMCs also asking additional discounts on RTP

scores.rationale: Capital barriers are enormous (Rs 36,354 cr for 9 MMT), new capacity is planned years ahead against demand, and pricing is formula-based rather than discount-driven, so competition is rational.
scores.quote: when people put up large capacities, long-term investment, it is based on long-term demand projection

scores.rationale: The southern MS shortfall implies product flowing in from other regions that CPCL can displace, but its peers are large well-run refiners, not weak donators.
scores.quote: in MS products are moving from other market to here. So, that is how we have made constant effort to increase our production of MS

scores.rationale: A modest, low-profile single-site PSU refiner that until recently held infrequent calls and lacked investor presentations, trading below book value by investors' own account.
scores.quote: The last concall I think probably done was like more than a year ago... the stock should not be substantially below book value

scores.rationale: Zero image or taste-based pricing power — realisations are set by international parity cracks and gross margins swing with the cycle ($8.64 to $4.22 to $9.2/bbl GRM in three years).
scores.quote: every $1-$2 of crack impacts the profit because there is a constant operating cost. So, I think taking a guess on the cracks will not be feasible

scores.rationale: Reliability is genuinely valued — 1,884 fire-free days, first-quartile Solomon operational availability, and stepping up LPG supply when national availability tightened — but the buyer still pays a formula price.
scores.quote: With global uncertainties affecting the availability of LPG all over the world, CPCL is happy to step up the requirement when the nation needed it

scores.rationale: Physical proximity to IOCL's facilities, direct RLNG pipeline connectivity and coastal location on international sea routes give genuine logistical convenience, though no sales force advantage.
scores.quote: close to our coast, is a RLNG terminal and we are connected to it directly through pipelines. The southern coast is close to the international sea route

scores.rationale: Almost entirely a corporate/captive B2B model where reliability of supply matters, but the RTP contract means no TCO premium is captured, and the new retail outlet push is small and unproven.
scores.quote: Even our retail outlet endeavor for which we had taken 300 licenses has started

scores.rationale: Process engineering strength is real (DCU utilisation from ~70% to near 100%, distillate yield to 79.1%, first-quartile Solomon) but this is operational optimisation of licensed refining units, not proprietary multi-product technology.
scores.quote: the DCU, Delayed Coker Unit, till now, I was operating at a capacity of 70-odd percent. This time, I'm close to 100%

scores.rationale: No discussion of any network or platform dynamic in a commodity refining business.
Access to IOCL's national distribution network plus adjacent evacuation infrastructure is a reach rivals cannot easily replicate, but it belongs to the parent rather than to CPCL itself.
scores.quote: We have a tie-up with them, we've a long-term agreement with them for selling

scores.rationale: Expansion is real (115→211 branches, 49 project offices) and growth-oriented rather than maintenance, but management explicitly frames capex as immaterial — a branch costs Rs 3-5 lakh and tech is opex — so there is no evidence of high, rising growth capex compounding at high incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: on the tech side, nothing major on the capex; however, opex is the only thing... average cost of each new branch... ranges somewhere between INR 3,00,000 to INR 5,00,000

scores.rationale: A&P spend is never quantified or discussed across the five calls; the only passing reference is to 'digital marketing channels' for the Gold ETF NFO.
scores.quote: as the market grows and we penetrate to the branch network and digital marketing channels

scores.rationale: There is an in-house tech team that has shipped FinX, Choice Money and Choice Connect and a lower-CAC digital acquisition stack, but management claims only parity with competitors and books tech as opex with no R&D quantum or efficiency disclosed.
scores.quote: our technology is no less than any other competitor in the industry

scores.rationale: A steady stream of small, complementary bolt-ons (Arete, Paisabuddy/Sureworth, Ayoleeza, Fintoo, Glory, Optimo) funded from internal accruals, with group EBITDA margin rising from 32.1% in FY25 to 37% in FY26 and the acquired Paisabuddy book performing in line — but deal economics and acquiree quality are never disclosed and the pace is high.
scores.quote: we have done a couple of acquisitions over the recent years and we intend to continue the same... we have enough internal accruals to support that

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or capital-return policy is mentioned in any of the five calls.

The model is increasingly balance-sheet-heavy — an Rs 800 Cr NBFC loan book, an Rs 370-400 Cr MTF book targeted to 'grow very aggressively', and Rs 677 Cr of debt — against Rs 1,145 Cr revenue, with no protecting moat to defend returns on that capital.
scores.quote: currently we are maintaining an average book of roughly around between INR 370 to INR 400 crores... Our target is to grow the MTF book very aggressively

scores.rationale: Runway is genuinely large (ADTO share only ~1.2%) and there is real evidence of capture — top-five in net client addition per NSE UCC while larger players shed clients — though the share gain itself is described as marginal and demat growth is decelerating (29%→24%→16% YoY).
scores.quote: Choice Broking has been one of the top five brokers which has seen a net client addition as per the NSE's active UCC list

scores.rationale: Credible, on-track domestic expansion — branches taken from 115 to 211 with the 100-branch FY26 target met, a stated five-year plan to cover ~800 districts, and Ayoleeza acquired specifically for state credentials in new geographies — but it is entirely within India with no premium brand travelling.
scores.quote: we are planning to have our own branch office at almost all districts, which are roughly around 800 districts across India

scores.rationale: Management attributes growth explicitly to volumes and client additions rather than pricing, with yield compression acknowledged in the NBFC book; the only mix benefit cited is the debt-to-equity MF shift.
scores.quote: our business is largely driven by the volumes, even in the volatile market, the volume has remained on an upward trajectory

scores.rationale: Mixed cycle position — the microfinance/unsecured credit cycle appears to be bottoming and derivative-regulation headwinds are being absorbed, but retail broking volumes are riding an elevated participation cycle, not a trough.
scores.quote: This rise was largely driven by the overall economic impacts which we had seen in the microfinance segment, but now things seem to be normalizing

scores.rationale: The end markets — financialisation of Indian household savings, MSME formalisation and credit-gap lending, and semi-urban/rural financial inclusion — are in genuine secular expansion, and management identifies the shift as structural rather than cyclical.
scores.quote: a clear equitization of household savings, where capital is steadily migrating from physical assets into financial markets... This shift is not cyclical, it's structural

scores.rationale: Growth leans heavily on continuous inorganic activity (at least six acquisitions across two years with more 'actively in discussion') alongside Rs 677 Cr of debt and a leveraged NBFC/MTF book, which is the opposite of the organic, low-leverage profile the parameter seeks.
scores.quote: on the acquisition also, we are open to discuss opportunities with various other players in the industry... we are actively in discussion with a couple of such companies

scores.rationale: There is a consistently articulated long-horizon thesis (phygital model in Tier-3/4, 800-district branch plan, AMC built passive-first over multiple years) and they have delivered against stated targets like the 100-branch FY26 goal, though heavy board/MD/CFO churn over FY22-FY25 tempers the independence claim.
scores.quote: once we are settled down with passive in the next one year, we will start active also in FY27

scores.rationale: A decade-old company that only held its maiden earnings call in April 2025, operates deliberately in semi-urban and Tier-3 markets, and delegates most of the commentary to the IR head rather than a celebrity promoter.
scores.quote: Thank you for joining us today for our first ever earnings conference call

scores.rationale: A segment-CEO structure and new functional hires (Deputy CEO AMC, CPTO, CFO) indicate a broadening bench, but there is no systematic talent-development programme described and the five-year history shows repeated senior exits (Chairman, two MDs, CFO).
scores.quote: We have dedicated CEOs for all the segments and all business verticals

scores.rationale: They do explain adverse items plainly (23% wealth AUM decline from debt redemptions, corporate insurance contraction, NPA spike from microfinance, first-ever QoQ order-book decline), but the tone is promotional, risk questions are waved away, and basic metrics are repeatedly unavailable.
scores.quote: I mean, we don't foresee anything going wrong from here. It's only a positive upward trend which we foresee from here

scores.rationale: Headline results (FY26 PAT +46%) are hard to separate from a favourable retail-participation cycle and a string of acquisitions — the 793%/328% wealth AUM 'growth' is largely the Arete purchase, and margin expansion is operating leverage on a market upcycle, so skill is not cleanly demonstrable.
scores.quote: Under Wealth Product Distribution, we have an AUM of Rs. 5,500 Cr plus, a growth of 793% on YoY basis

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in any market or in the customer's mind — ~1.2% ADTO share in a fragmented broking industry and a sub-Rs 1,000 Cr NBFC in a crowded MSME lending market.
scores.quote: With Demat account at 1.23 million and ADTO market share steady at 1.2%

scores.rationale: Some stickiness is claimed from physical handholding and secured LAP relationships, but broking accounts carry minimal switching costs and management itself has to run activation campaigns on dormant demat holders.
scores.quote: what are we doing to convert dormant demat holders into active traders

scores.rationale: Retail broking in India is fragmented and price-competitive with powerful discount incumbents, and management concedes it faces the same regulatory headwinds as everyone else; the customer has full negotiating power.
scores.quote: how we are placed against competitors like Angel One and Motilal Oswal

scores.rationale: Low structural barriers and regulatory volatility (derivatives/expiry changes) characterise the industry, with the company's own defence being physical presence rather than any entry barrier, and ownership at the top has been unstable across FY22-FY25.
scores.quote: there are certain impact in the overall industry and we will also face certain headwinds

scores.rationale: There are identifiable weak hands to take share from — larger brokers losing active clients, stressed unsecured/microfinance lenders, and small players seeking to consolidate into Choice.
scores.quote: the overall industry has seen a decline or the larger players have seen a decline in the active clients

scores.rationale: The deliberate Tier-3/Tier-4 semi-urban niche served by physical branches is precisely the segment digital-first, capital-rich competitors have ignored, and the company itself stayed off the IR radar until FY25.
scores.quote: We are largely bullish on the new entrants in the financial services space, which are going to come from Tier 3 and below geographies only

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; the offering is commoditised financial distribution where the company concedes yield compression as it moves to prime borrowers and competes against zero/low-brokerage players.
scores.quote: a slight decline in the average interest rate will also be there

scores.rationale: The core proposition to underserved Tier-3 customers is trust and reliability delivered through a physical presence and full-journey handholding rather than price, which the company positions as its primary differentiator versus digital rivals.
scores.quote: people require a physical presence of the platform providers through whom the people are investing their hard-earned money

scores.rationale: Accessibility is the genuine strength — 67,000 Choice Business Associates, 211 branches, 49 project offices, an in-house physical collections team, and a mandate to plug into India Post Payments Bank's 1.6 lakh outlets and 12 crore customers.
scores.quote: our 65,000 plus Choice Business Associate continue to be our trust bridge, allowing us to maintain high-touch relationships in a high-tech world

scores.rationale: Benefit-to-customer matching is only partly right: retail is served with convenience and assurance rather than any intangible brand pull, while the corporate side (corporate insurance, government advisory) shows weak lock-in with a contract lost and premiums declining two quarters running.
scores.quote: there has been one contract which we could not renew during the quarter because of which we have seen a decline

scores.rationale: Technology is positioned as an enabler at parity with peers, not an edge — no meaningful tech capex, total broking tech spend of about Rs 10 Cr in a quarter, and the business model is explicitly physical-first.
scores.quote: business model largely remains on the physical presence, which is supported by the technology

scores.rationale: Nothing in the model is self-reinforcing across two sides; growth comes from adding branches, associates and acquired books, and cross-sell/LTV ambitions are stated as a plan rather than an operating network effect.
scores.quote: we should have an ecosystem where we can create a higher LTV using multiple products

scores.rationale: Distribution and on-ground service reach is the company's most defensible asset — 67,000 associates plus 211 branches in geographies digital brokers do not serve, in-house physical collections, and now access to India Post Payments Bank's unmatched last-mile network.
scores.quote: India Post itself has 1.6 lakh post offices, 1.8 lakh postmen... this is technically the largest distribution system across India

scores.rationale: As a lender its 'growth capex' is distribution and new-vertical build-out, which has been heavy and rising (gold loan launched into 118 branches, housing expanding out of the south, headcount to ~65,000) while ROE held at 19-23%, though incremental returns are diluted by elevated credit costs.
scores.quote: The newly introduced gold loan business disbursed INR772 crores during Q3 FY '26 operating out of 118 dedicated branches in the South and Eastern parts of India.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend in any of the excerpts.

No formal R&D, but a sustained analytics/underwriting-tool programme and a steady cadence of new product lines (CSEL, SBPL, gold loan, D2C digital) show investment that yields new products and customers.
scores.quote: We have been working on improving our underwriting tool, specifically the Gini coefficient... This initiative has been in place for the past year and has already helped us improve asset quality across CSEL, CD, and the Vehicle Finance segments

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed across the four years of excerpts; growth is entirely organic.

Distribution policy is consistent but token (INR1.30 interim plus INR0.70 final for FY26) with no buybacks, and capital is being taken in rather than returned via CCD conversions, which is coherent for a growth lender but not shareholder-distribution quality.
scores.quote: the Board approved the payment of an interim dividend of 65%, which is INR1.30 per share

scores.rationale: A balance-sheet lender running 6-7x debt/equity is structurally asset-heavy, the opposite of the asset-light-plus-moat combination the parameter seeks.
scores.quote: We are currently in the six times debt equity levels. We will continue to be around the 6 to 7 times levels

scores.rationale: Repeated, quantified share capture with plenty of runway left: AUM compounded from INR86,703 crore (Q1FY23) to INR2,42,630 crore (Q4FY26) and FY26 segment growth ran far ahead of industry.
scores.quote: industry grew by 20%, but Chola grew by 56% in heavy commercial vehicle... the market is actually growing at the rate of, say, 16%, we grew by 28%

scores.rationale: Credible domestic geographic widening — housing finance moving out of its southern base, gold loan branches opened across South and East, and deep Tier 3-5 town coverage — but it is within-India expansion, not a premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: housing finance is also expanding out of south. So, they are also recruiting people.

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/AUM-led with margin gains coming from RBI rate cuts rather than pricing power, though there is a genuine positive mix shift toward higher-yield gold loan, SBPL and consumer durables.
scores.quote: NIM improved by 33 bps in Q3 over previous year with the RBI's rate cut progressively impacting our cost of funds favourably

scores.rationale: The company is positioned right at a cyclical trough with an identifiable upturn: two years of vehicle-finance credit stress, with NCL falling 2.2%→2.1%→2.0% through FY26 and demand re-igniting on GST and rate cuts.
scores.quote: Vehicle demand has improved after the GST rate cut... we are expecting quarter 4 of the vehicle finance is going to be very good

scores.rationale: Retail and MSME credit penetration in India is in secular expansion, evidenced by 20-34% AUM growth sustained across the entire four-year window through both stress and recovery.
scores.quote: AUM growth remained healthy at 21% as at the end of the quarter, reflecting sustained momentum across the portfolio

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth with an explicit, honoured leverage/capital discipline and a counter-cyclical INR200 crore precautionary overlay, tempered by the inherent 6-7x leverage and CCD-funded capital.
scores.quote: unless the Tier I one goes down below 13%, we will not be seeking capital. I think we stick to that stance.

scores.rationale: Management set out a multi-year plan to exit fintech partnership lending and executed it over three years despite the visible growth drag, and is grinding through a multi-year quality upgrade of the CSEL sourcing book.
scores.quote: We have already come down to 3 partners from 10 partners in the last 2 years' time... we segregated the entire portfolio into 4 category, diamond, gold, silver and bronze

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently data-dense and unpromotional, with the Chairman handing detail to business heads rather than personalising performance, though Chola is a well-covered large-cap followed by every major broker.
scores.quote: As of now, we should not use this strong and all. It will be better than quarter 3, definitely.

scores.rationale: Evidence of an internal pipeline — Kundu promoted from Executive Director to MD & CEO, and multiple named business heads (Balraj Menon, Ranjit Ramachandran, Sucheth Bharathan, Prashanth) field questions directly — but no explicit talent-development system is described.
scores.quote: their target of ROA of 4.5%, pretax ROA, Prashanth has been always saying that he will deliver it. So, we should actually rely on his commitment

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly volunteers unflattering detail, refuses to over-claim, and explicitly flags where its accounting is more conservative than peers'.
scores.quote: 6.4% is very high... in some of the players, we have seen that they do it slightly differently. They basically take income also into the NCL line and keep the NCL better. But we have not done that.

scores.rationale: Recent improvement is substantially macro-driven (GST rate cut, RBI cuts lowering cost of funds) and the ROA has been stuck at 2.3-3.3% through the stress years, so skill is only partly separable from cycle and leverage.
scores.quote: NIMs improved by 40 bps year-on-year in Q4 driven by a gradual reduction in the Company's cost of funds as interest rates softened

scores.rationale: Retail lending offers no monopoly of mind or captive aftermarket — management describes competing directly with banks and other NBFCs for the same borrowers.
scores.quote: the strategy customer or group customer or top of the pyramid customer or large fleet operator customers are always being funded by banks only

scores.rationale: There is a partial structural niche — small road transport operators and sub-INR20 lakh tickets in Tier 3-5 towns that banks avoid — but borrowers face negligible switching costs.
scores.quote: The lower tonnage vehicle is still is actually getting sold in the Tier 3, Tier 4, Tier 5 town... they are mainly the market load operator where the NBFC is only financing.

scores.rationale: Vehicle and mortgage finance in India is a fragmented field of banks, NBFCs and fintechs, and pricing is set by competitive cost-of-funds rather than by a stable few.
scores.quote: your vehicle credit cost is running at 2%, which is relatively higher versus the peers

scores.rationale: Low entry barriers are evidenced by the fintech partnership wave Chola itself joined and then had to unwind, and by banks pushing into segments as funding costs allow.
scores.quote: Due to the withdrawal from fin-tech-based lending, the growth year-on-year continues to be negative over Q3 of FY '25.

scores.rationale: Weak lenders exist to donate share — the fintech/small-ticket unsecured cohort blew up and banks stay out of the retail SRTO segment, allowing Chola to grow well above industry in HCV and SCV.
scores.quote: SRTO were away from the market earlier because they were not seeing the capacity utilization... So, our disbursement growth is not depending on whether bank is aggressive or not.

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a large listed NBFC with quarterly calls covered by Kotak, Citi, CLSA, Morgan Stanley, DSP, Ambit and others.
scores.quote: hosted by Kotak Securities Limited

scores.rationale: Credit is a commodity here; there is no image- or taste-driven pricing power, and yields are set by segment risk and funding cost rather than brand.
scores.quote: So, ticket size is INR 2 lakh now. It had started with INR 300,000, it has come down. And yield has gone up now to 15.

scores.rationale: Some relationship-based reliability value in serving small operators through downturns, but nothing in the calls shows customers paying up for certainty over price.
scores.quote: We were always financing the retail customer

scores.rationale: Accessibility and direct customer intimacy are the core proposition — a ~65,000-person on-ground sales and collection force reaching Tier 3-5 towns that banks do not serve.
scores.quote: 31,000 is collection now.

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched to the customer — convenience, speed and doorstep service for retail SRTO and MSME borrowers — with risk managed by collateral and CGTMSE cover rather than by brand.
scores.quote: As of now, we have covered around 70 percentage of our assets. And we continue to improve that.

scores.rationale: Real but modest technology work — underwriting Gini improvement and an in-house digital/D2C platform — that supports underwriting rather than constituting a deep multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: direct-to-customer financing through our in-house digital and fintech platform

scores.rationale: Sourcing is through dealers, DSAs and branches with no self-reinforcing two-sided network; scale brings distribution reach, not network economics.
scores.quote: which is like on-ground DSA, DST business

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the genuine moat — branch-led origination across MSME and mortgages plus deep rural vehicle presence and a large collections field force that banks and fintechs cannot replicate.
scores.quote: The MSME segment... recorded 11% growth in Q4 disbursements supported by strong demand and robust branch-led distribution.

scores.rationale: No meaningful growth-capex programme is evident across the four calls; the only growth investment named is a sales app launched in FY26 explicitly to reach parity with rivals, while ROE fell to 10.4% versus the 16-18% ambition.
scores.quote: this app will put us on par with the new age companies in terms of the digital offerings

scores.rationale: A&P jumped to Rs.183 crores (21-22% of NWP) in FY22 on IPL/Delhi Metro/FM spends yet was later cut back as part of EOM 'belt tightening' with no durable pricing power or brand premium to show for it.
scores.quote: Chola MS associated itself with RCB in the IPL, so there were some related advertising costs

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or product-innovation pipeline is discussed in any of the excerpts.
No acquisitions are mentioned across the four calls; the structure is unchanged (Chola Finance, Chola MS, Chola MS Risk JV).
There is a stated, rationally-explained policy of retaining earnings to fund growth and solvency, but no buybacks and the retention is capital-necessity driven with solvency slipping to 1.96x.
scores.quote: Shareholders have been considered not to take a dividend. So the money is getting flowed back into the business to support growth and solvency level.

scores.rationale: The float-leverage model that was 'one of the highest in the industry' has deteriorated, with investment leverage falling from ~6.2x to 5.5x and solvency from 2.18x to 1.96x, and there is no moat protecting the returns.
scores.quote: our kind of a leverage, which used to be 6 plus -- 6.2% say, last year, it has dropped to 5.5%

scores.rationale: As a ~5% motor player Chola MS has ample runway and grew OD share to 5.89%, but overall motor share was flat at 5.2-5.25% across FY26 and direct premium actually declined on the Rs.590 crore crop loss.
scores.quote: our market share in the OD has been growing up and TP has been moderated... grew the motor OD market share to about 5.89%

scores.rationale: Regional leadership in Tamil Nadu/Chhattisgarh and improvement in AP-Telangana were cited in 2022, but the only later geographic news is losing crop business on retender in Maharashtra, Bengal and Odisha.
scores.quote: maintain its leadership position in Tamil Nadu and Chhattisgarh and bettering its performance in Andhra and Telangana

scores.rationale: Pricing is the binding constraint rather than a driver — motor TP prices have been frozen by the regulator for four years and OD is under discount-led competition, forcing the company to shrink 2-wheeler volumes to protect economics.
scores.quote: the continued absence of increase in motor third-party premium for the last 3 to 4 years

scores.rationale: The company is visibly near a cyclical trough — combined ratio 115.2%, ROE 10.4% — with several identifiable upturn levers: a pending TP price hike, the nationwide crop retender it will re-enter, EOM glide path completed, and IFRS discounting benefit from FY28.
scores.quote: next year, we will have a new season tender, which will be across the country... which should bring back the profitability

scores.rationale: Indian general insurance remains a structurally under-penetrated, fast-growing end market, with industry growth of 22.3% and private-sector growth of 33% cited in the earliest call.
scores.quote: Q1 FY2023 witnessed an industry growth of 22.3% and the private sector grew by 33%

scores.rationale: Management has stayed organic with no M&A, deliberately walked away from unprofitable volume (2-wheeler book cut from 19.6% to 10.6%, group health avoided), refused to chase top line, and retained earnings to protect solvency.
scores.quote: we are very clear that we won't be chasing top line. So the inherent economic viability of the business is what will drive our appetite.

scores.rationale: Reserving motor TP 10-14% above peers and pruning a profitable-looking 2-wheeler book to protect liabilities four years out are costly, independent long-term calls taken against short-term reported-earnings pressure.
scores.quote: Chola MS continues to be prudent and conservative in its provisioning for motor TP losses with the level of provisioning -- booked 10% higher than many of its peers

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the MD and CFO with dense operational detail, no promotional framing, and the handover praise for the outgoing MD is brief and understated.
scores.quote: My heartfelt thanks to all the analysts for their incisive queries and comments, which has kept us on our toes

scores.rationale: Both key succession events in FY26 were filled from outside — the CFO hired from the Aditya Birla Group and the incoming MD an external 'industry veteran' — with no evidence of an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: Santosh joined us in the month of August 2025 and comes with the prior experience with the Aditya Birla Group

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly volunteers bad news and owns underperformance versus peers, quantifying each drag (TP reserving 3.05%, fire claims 1.78%, crop loss Rs.590 crores) and admitting its OD delta is worse than the industry's.
scores.quote: the current year in terms of the claims ratio, I should admit has been bad for us... for us the delta has been about 10%

scores.rationale: The quality of disclosure and the prudence narrative sit alongside repeatedly missed outcomes — ROE guided at 12.5-13% in FY23 and an ambition of 16-18% versus 10.4% delivered in FY26 — so the candour should not be read as evidence of superior underwriting skill.
scores.quote: we had discussed earlier our ambition to sustain ROEs in the 16% to 18% range. Given the current non-annualized ROE at 8%

scores.rationale: With ~5.25% motor share and 3.3% overall market share, Chola MS holds no monopoly-like position in any customer's mind or aftermarket.
scores.quote: In motor, the principal line of business, the market share stood at 5.25%

scores.rationale: General insurance policies are annually renewable with negligible switching costs — management is building an app precisely to lift renewal rates — and the crop retender showed business can be lost wholesale overnight.
scores.quote: the focus will now be on pushing up the renewal rate

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented and price-competitive rather than a stable oligopoly, with Chola at 3.3% share facing heavy discounting and payouts and losing tendered business to a public insurer.
scores.quote: the competitive intensity in the market is quite high with the kind of discounts and payouts

scores.rationale: Pricing is visibly irrational — industry-wide motor OD loss ratios rose 6-7% on competitive intensity, commissions/payouts are high enough that the regulator is being asked to cap them, and crop retenders cleared at value-destroying prices.
scores.quote: Motor OD claims ratio has been higher and also reflects the competitive intensity in the industry

scores.rationale: Rather than facing weak competitors to take share from, Chola MS was the donor — surrendering Rs.590 crores of crop premium to AIC and running an OD loss-ratio deterioration worse than peers.
scores.quote: business has shifted more from the private sector players to AIC to a larger extent, at least in Maharashtra

scores.rationale: The listed holding company itself is thinly covered (a handful of analysts on each call), but Indian general insurance is a heavily capitalised, well-followed sector rather than an ignored niche.
scores.quote: as there are no further questions, I now hand the conference over to the management

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power: the product is a commoditised motor policy sold on discount, and the company has been underwriting at a 112-115% combined ratio.
scores.quote: the combined ratio for the year was at 115.2% and 112.2% without the 1/n effect

scores.rationale: Claims-handling capability is a genuine differentiator — an industry-leading compromise-settlement franchise saving over 50% of average severity — but it accrues to the insurer's costs, not to a price premium from customers who buy on discount.
scores.quote: Chola MS is one of the leaders in the compromise settlement and can save more than 50% level in terms of average severity

scores.rationale: Distribution intimacy is being built deliberately: growth in OEM and financial channels, a scaled agency base, and the Chola Xceed app for structured partner engagement and agent productivity management.
scores.quote: over the years, we have also seen the growth in agency coming up... This app will help us build a very structured partner engagement

scores.rationale: The book is dominated by retail motor where the required intangible pricing power is absent, while the corporate/commercial lines where reliability lock-in could apply remain sub-scale and are being entered on unattractive pricing.
scores.quote: the underlying pricing component in the commercial side is not something that we would have liked

scores.rationale: The flagship technology initiative is explicitly a catch-up to reach parity with digital-first rivals, not a multi-product lead, and it appears only in the final call of the four-year window.
scores.quote: We feel that this app will put us on par with the new age companies in terms of the digital offerings

scores.rationale: No self-reinforcing network exists — the channel-partner app is a productivity tool aimed at renewal rates, and scale has not protected loss ratios, which deteriorated more than peers'.
scores.quote: When it is 6% to 7% for others, we have had an 8% to 9% increase in ours

scores.rationale: A credible multi-channel reach (top-5 private motor player, agency plus OEM and financial channels, strong regional presence) but nothing rivals cannot match, as flat share and lost tenders demonstrate.
scores.quote: we've been fairly steady in terms of the market share and being amongst the top 5 private sector players in the motor business

scores.rationale: Sustained order-backed growth capex across all verticals (Hosur, stampings, aluminium, composites, iron castings export line) at a disciplined ~5%-of-sales envelope, but incremental returns have been slow to show as RONA slipped to 18.4% and several funded orders were delayed for years.
scores.quote: Growth capex was INR2.3 billion, concentrated mainly in India. Overall capex was INR3.8 billion, which is within our norms of 5% of sales.

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotion spend across the 17 calls; as a Tier-1 OEM supplier it has no consumer brand programme discussed.

Consistent application engineering yields a visible pipeline of new products and order wins (fuel rails, EV housings, high-tonnage machined castings, 2W crankshafts), though no R&D spend or efficiency metric is ever disclosed and EV programmes repeatedly slipped.
scores.quote: we are developing low -pressure fabricated fuel rails for petrol and CNG vehicles as well as large fully finished precision forgings for vehicle drivelines
